Today I received some new MVP/Axiom discs to test out. Since it was late, I didn't get to film them, and only had a handful of throws with each mold. Keep that in mind, as my feelings may change as I learn the nuances of each mold.

Axiom Virus

The Virus surprised me. The Virus is described as a broken in Impulse, and as you can see in the Impulse test video I found that mold very understable. From the four throws I had with the Virus, they seemed closest to the more overstable green Impulse I was throwing in that video.

They are definitely understable, but they didn't seem to show any more turn than last time I threw the Impulse. Either way this driver has a significant amount of glide for me. Like the Insanity, the amount of high speed turn it had felt controllable. I didn't feel like I had to put ridiculous amounts of hyzer on it for a powered down straight shot or full power S flight. That being said, this isn't a driver I can throw full power and flat, it turns too hard and too early. This is no surprise since the Impulse is the same way for me.

This was a disc I did not expect to like because I generally don't bag very understable molds. I never bagged an Impulse for example. However, after throwing them a few times in the field, I'm going to have to try them out head to head against my Insanity and see what I think. If I do bag it, it would compliment the Insanity for it, not replace it.

I didn't try any pure distance lines tonight, just some controlled golf lines. Had no issue pushing it to 450' on a hyzer flip, and I'd expect 500' during a full length field test with them.

The Virus completes the first set of Axiom distance drivers. I've become a big fan of these molds (Fireball, Wrath, Insanity, Virus) largely because of the softer blend of Neutron / Proton they're available in.

MVP Wave

The Wave is the second 21.5mm distance driver from MVP. The first was the Photon, which I'll write about next. These discs are about a 12-12.5 on the Innova speed scale for reference, but they move surprisingly fast in the air IMO.

The Wave matches the description on the MVP site perfectly. Longer Inertia. The flight felt familiar from the first throw, and as someone that's been throwing Inertias and the Insanity since their release, I can tell this disc will have a very short learning curve.

The Wave shows high speed turn for me. Thrown hard, flat and low, it would turn over and hold it to the ground, though it doesn't turn over quite as hard as the Impulse, Virus or my intentionally seasoned Insanity. Thrown hard, flat and fairly high, it would turn over, penetrate forward, then have a late, sweeping fade.

Where this disc shined for me was a hard hyzer flip drive. It has enough high speed turn to fly a nice distance S line, but enough resistance to turning over hard that I can really lay into it.

Like the Virus, this mold shows a lot of glide. I'm excited to spend more time with this mold, because I can see myself bagging this to compliment my Photons I've been throwing since their release. It will be the more understable distance counterpart to my 155-161g Photons, while the Neutron Photons will be my moderately OS Distance drivers.

These were flying further than the other two discs for me, unsurprisingly. I get my longest throws hyzer flipping something a bit understable like the Wave. I'd put my longer throws in the 480-510' range, and they may dethrone my 146g Fission Photon for my longest recorded throw when I get a chance to really figure them out.

MVP Neutron Photon

This was the disc I was most excited for. I've been bagging a pair of Fission Photos since they came out. 161g as a stable distance driver (Pretty much just holds whatever release angle I give it) and a 146g Photon for absolute max D, tailwind bombs, big turnovers etc.

Right off the bat these reminded me of Teslas. No matter how hard I threw them, on a flat release they just wanted to go straight then fade, no turning over. They remind me of a flat, beefy Destroyer. I am very pleased with this, because this is a distance driver I plan to cycle. Starting out this OS will let them cover all my distance needs if I want, between the 140's Fissions and these beefy max weights.

To get a good distance line I was having to throw them hard, low and with a little anhyzer. They'd ride this release angle about 80-85% of the flight, pushing forward remarkably fast, then fight out and finish straight a head as they hyzer to the ground.

Forehands were the same story. I could rip them as hard as I wanted with a flat release, and they resisted turn every time. Thrown hard and with some anhyzer, they'd show a lot of glide and the ability to consistently flex back to a hyzer finish.

I'm really happy with this disc. For raw distance, the Fission Photons and the Wave will be the better choice, but the max weight Neutron Photons is going to be an incredibly reliable line shaper on the course for me.

Additionally, I received a 155g Proton Anode and some Plasma Nanos I'll be testing out :)

I'll have videos of all three molds posted soon!
